$comment: Central config for the /rca-build RCA harness. All formerly-hardcoded product/infra values live here. No kubectl/chitragupta/bifrost literals — connectors are discovered and probe-validated at the gate into the capability manifest (see skills/rca-build/references/evidence-routing.md). No reportFile: the plugin never writes a local RCA report — the full report lives on the Test Observability UI (triggerRcaReport).
$concurrencyComment: Max coordinator subagents run in parallel during Step 5 fan-out. HONORED LITERALLY on the default path (direct Agent-tool dispatch of ai-tfa-coordinator subagents — one message, up to `concurrency` tool-use blocks per batch) and by the sequential harness (lib/loop.mjs). Only a SOFT target on the opt-in Workflow-tool path (workflows/rca-batch.mjs), which the Workflow runtime hard-caps at min(16, cpu cores - 2) regardless of this value — that cap is architectural and cannot be raised from this repo. See SKILL.md Step 5.
$softPendingDrainComment: tfaRcaTurn abandons its in-call poll at pollSoftPendingMs (90s) and returns a soft PENDING while the TFA agent keeps working — turns finalizing past 90s are routine. On a soft PENDING the loop READS the same turnId via getTfaTurnResult on this budget before it routes asks or submits anything further; reads do not consume turnCap. Only when the budget is spent does the run end PENDING (pending-resume row).
$maxErrorReadsComment: A soft PENDING is drained on the full budget below, but a HARD read failure (a thrown error, or a result whose status/message says the TFA agent run failed) is a different signal: it will not resolve by asking again. After this many CONSECUTIVE failed reads the drain stops early and the row ends PENDING with a `tfa-error` note, still resumable. A single good read clears the streak. Measured motivation: on one real build, drain reads plus their sleeps were 23% of all coordinator tool calls, and the four tests that wedged this way were the four slowest in the batch.

paths.$comment: State CSV path is ALWAYS derived per build via lib/csv-state.mjs csvPathFor(buildId, stateDir): the build id is in the filename (no cross-build collisions) and the default directory is OS temp (<tmpdir>/bstack-rca/), so the harness never pollutes the invoking workspace. Set stateDir only to retain the CSV somewhere specific (e.g. a CI artifact dir).

$capabilitiesComment: The capability table (R7). Keyed by CAPABILITY, joined to evidenceRouting by capability name — deliberately a sibling block, not rows inside evidenceRouting. buildManifest() enumerates Object.values(evidenceRouting) and reads entry.capability off every value, so a capability-keyed row placed in there becomes an evidenceType entry, and a row naming a new capability injects a phantom manifest entry that unavailableCapabilities() then reports to the user and to TFA as a missing connector. Nothing enumerates top-level config keys, so a sibling is safe. The capability set is derived from evidenceRouting and is exactly {github, infra, logs, metrics, other} — ci/product_code/deploy are evidenceTypes routing to github, k8s routes to infra, and test_logs carries no capability at all.
$probeComment: Probes are validated by isProbeRunnable() in lib/tool-cache.mjs, NOT by isRunnable(). isRunnable exists to judge cacheability: it allows pipelines into ALLOWED_FILTER (which includes python3, awk, sed) and restricts leaders to gh/kubectl/curl/git — so it both permits `curl X | python3` and refuses `docker ps`. Probe rules instead: one command, no pipeline, no operators, no redirects, no mutation, and a leader present in BOTH the global catalog and this row's own fingerprint executables. Placeholders are brace-form {field}; an unquoted < is read as a file redirect and rejected.

baseBranch.consumer: merged-PR window for the culprit hunt (Step 4 gh pr list --search merged:from..to)

runtimeKind.consumer: which infra probe applies at all (Gate Part A records the KIND in the manifest)

namespace.consumer: kubectl scope for Step 4 per-workload sweeps

workloads.consumer: failure-signature to workload routing for Step 4 log sweeps

serviceNames.consumer: failure-signature to service mapping for the log sweep

metricsNamespace.consumer: memory/CPU pressure lookup during evidence gathering

other.$comment: The catch-all for a stack discovery cannot classify. By definition it has nothing to fingerprint, so it declares no fingerprints, probe, mcpProbe or scopeProbe — permitted because resolvable is always-asked. exemptFromDiscoveryReport keeps it out of the user-facing 'not available' line: it can never match a fingerprint, so reporting it every run would be noise. The manifest and the TFA-facing declaration still mark it unavailable.
